desc:
AI workflow monitoring and error alerts show you how your automations are really performing. Ecom Swift LLC adds counts, delay tracking and alerts to your workflows, so a failure reaches you before it reaches a customer.

## What is workflow monitoring?

Workflow monitoring is the practice of counting what your automations do and warning you when the numbers look wrong. It tracks how many runs happened, how many succeeded, how many failed and how long each took. When a figure crosses a limit you set, an alert goes to email or chat.

Monitoring answers one question: is the workflow still doing its job today? That is a different question from what happened in a specific case, which a log answers.

## Why silent failures are the worst kind

Automations rarely fail loudly. A connection expires, a form field changes, an account runs out of credit, and the workflow quietly stops. Orders are not routed, replies are not drafted, leads are not saved. Nobody notices until a customer complains.

A manual process at least looks broken when it breaks. An automated one looks fine from the outside, which is why somebody has to watch it.

## How monitoring improves results

The first gain is speed. An alert on the first failed run lets you repair the problem in minutes, while the damage is small. The second gain is confidence. When you can see success counts every day, you can trust the workflow with more work.

Trends add insight. A slow rise in waiting time points to a bottleneck. A cluster of errors with the same cause points to one fix that clears many failures. Grouped error reasons turn a long list of problems into a short list of tasks.

## What a good monitoring setup includes

- A daily count of runs, successes and failures.
- Time taken per run, with a clear definition of slow.
- Alerts by email or chat when a run fails.
- Alert limits that you choose and can change.
- A weekly summary of how the workflow performed.
- A dashboard of trends in a tool you already use.
- Error reasons grouped together.
- A checklist for fixing common problems.
- A plain explanation of what each figure means.

## What we do

We list the workflows you want watched and agree on what healthy looks like for each: how many runs per day, how long a run should take, what counts as a failure. Then we add the counting and timing steps, connect the alerts and build a dashboard in a sheet or reporting tool in your account.

We test the alerts on purpose by triggering a failure, so you know they arrive. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of workflows, delay tracking, trend views and fix checklists. Monitoring shows problems, and repairs are a separate piece of work.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Set limits based on how the workflow behaves in a normal week.
- Send alerts to a place someone actually reads.
- Name one person who owns each alert.
- Review the weekly summary, even when it looks calm.
- Adjust limits after a few weeks of real data.

**Avoid:**
- Setting limits so tight that alerts arrive constantly.
- Sending every alert to a mailbox nobody checks.
- Ignoring repeated small errors.
- Watching only success counts and missing slow runs.
- Assuming a quiet dashboard means everything is fine without checking the run count.

## Who it is for

A store owner who relies on order or inventory automations can learn about a break quickly. A support team that uses automated routing can see when messages stop moving. An operations lead who inherited several workflows and has no view of them can finally see how they behave.

## What we need from you

Tell us which workflows to monitor, where you want alerts and who should receive them. Share a rough idea of normal volume. We never need passwords. You add us as a collaborator or limited team user in the tools involved, and you stay in control of every account.
